q: 1. If the formation level... has a uniform gradient... and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope...
explain: Earthwork volume can be calculated using any of these mathematical methods depending on the required accuracy and ground profile.

q: 2. To account for the corrugations, the plain area of the semi-corrugated asbestos sheet is increased (for white washing)
explain: For corrugated surfaces, the flat area is increased by a percentage (10% for semi-corrugated, 20% for corrugated) to account for the actual surface area being painted/washed.

q: 3. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
explain: The Prismoidal rule (Simpson's rule for volume) states V = D/3 [First + Last + 4(Sum of even areas) + 2(Sum of odd areas)].

q: 4. The area of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S : 1 and length L is
explain: Sloping breadth = √(d² + (Sd)²) = d√(1+S²). Area for one side = L * d√(1+S²).

q: 5. The cross section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is
explain: These formulas represent the areas of the cutting and banking portions respectively when a road traverses a side-sloping ground.

q: 6. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking, is
explain: This is the general formula for the cross-sectional area of a road on side-sloping ground where 'r' is the ground slope and 's' is the side slope.

q: 7. The item of the brick structure measured in sq. m, is
explain: Brick edging (as for pathways) or thin brick soling is measured in area (sq. m) or length (m), unlike structural brickwork which is cubic.

q: 8. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms are horizontal ledges left between the top of the cutting and the toe of the bank to improve stability and prevent siltation.

q: 9. The reduced levels of points, 30 metres apart along the longitudinal section of a road portion... is
explain: In surveying, chainage is recorded as 'Chain + Links'. For 30m intervals, 15 chains (if using 20m chain) or specific local link counts are used to designate the station.

q: 10. Pick up the excavation where measurement is made in square meters for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
explain: Shallow works like surface dressing (cleaning) and surface excavation (up to 30cm) are paid by area (m²) rather than volume.

q: 11. The cross-section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is shown in figure. The area of the shaded portion is
explain: This formula represents the cross-sectional area of a road in 'side-hill' work where one portion is in cut and another in fill, depending on the side slope (s) and transverse slope (r).

q: 12. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking shown in figure is
explain: This formula represents the area of a trapezoidal cross-section in an embankment (banking) when the original ground has a transverse slope 'r' and the side slopes are 's'.

q: 13. The cross-sectional area of the embankment of a canal fully in embankment (figure) is
explain: The area for a canal embankment is the sum of the two trapezoidal banks: Area = 2 × [bh + sh²]. If the top widths are b1 and b2, the formula simplifies to (b1 + b2)h + 2sh² (or sh² per side).

q: 14. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri etc. When depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm. is
explain: When the depth of excavation is shallow (less than 30 cm), it is treated as 'Surface Excavation' and measured in square meters (sq m) rather than volume.

q: 15. The unit of payment for blasting of rock including stacking is in
explain: The payment for explosives used in blasting is often calculated by weight (kg), though the excavation itself is usually cu m. In this context, the explosive material/effort is kg.

q: 16. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
the starting and end points of the curves
explain: Standard highway surveying requires cross-sections at regular intervals (usually 30m), at critical curve points, and always perpendicular to the center line for accurate volume calculation.

q: 17. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc. up to 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/ hard rock is in
explain: Small trenching for utilities (pipes/cables) at standardized depths is frequently paid per linear meter.

q: 18. The unit of payment for A.C. sheet roofing is in
explain: Sheet roofing (Asbestos Cement, GI, or tiles) is measured based on the superficial area covered, hence square meters (sq. m.).

q: 19. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: In plastering measurements, deductions are not made for small openings (up to 0.5 sqm) or for ends of structural members like beams and rafters to account for the extra labor of finishing edges.

q: 20. In a detailed estimate the provision for contingencies is usually
explain: Contingencies are incidental expenses of a miscellaneous character which cannot be reasonably predicted; 3% to 5% of the total estimate is reserved for this.

q: 21. Generally the provision for supervision is
explain: Supervision or work-charged establishment charges generally range from 5% to 10% to cover the cost of technical staff employed during construction.

q: 22. The useful part of livable area of a building is also known as
explain: Carpet area is the net usable area within the walls of a building where a carpet can be laid, excluding the thickness of inner walls, balconies, and common areas.

q: 23. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having no relationship with real damage, is known as
explain: Liquidated damages are a pre-estimated amount of compensation mentioned in the contract to be paid in case of a breach or delay, regardless of the actual loss.

q: 24. Thickness of plastering is usually
explain: Standard plastering for internal brick walls is usually 12 mm thick. Ceiling plaster is typically 6 mm, and external plaster is 18-20 mm.

q: 25. The term VAT is stands for
explain: VAT stands for Value Added Tax, which is a consumption tax placed on a product whenever value is added at each stage of the supply chain.

q: 26. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work is
explain: Quantity surveying is the professional task of taking off and calculating the physical volumes/areas of work from drawings.

q: 27. Revised estimate is warranted when the sanctions estimate exceeds, for whether reason, by more than
explain: Administrative and technical rules dictate that if the expenditure on a work is likely to exceed the original sanctioned amount by more than 5%, a revised estimate must be submitted for approval.

q: 28. In a galvanized corrugated iron sheet the pitch (center to center distance) of corrugation is usually
explain: The standard pitch for corrugations in GI sheets used in roofing is typically 75 mm (or 3 inches).

q: 29. The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: Standard AC corrugated sheets are manufactured with a width of 1.05 meters to allow for overlaps during installation.

q: 30. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: A P-trap outlet is designed with a specific downward slope (usually around 14 degrees) to ensure efficient drainage and maintain the water seal.

q: 31. The number of corrugations per sheet in case of Asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: Standard AC sheets commonly feature 7 corrugations (referred to as 7-corrugation sheets) for standard roofing applications.

q: 32. The concrete work for the following parts of the building of specified thickness is measured in square metres
explain: Damp Proof Course (D.P.C.) is measured in square metres because it is a thin layer with a specified thickness. Roof slabs and floors are typically measured in cubic metres unless they are very thin, but D.P.C. is the most standard answer here.

q: 33. Annual financial statement of the anticipated receipts and expenditures, is called
explain: A budget is a forward-looking financial plan that estimates income and expenses for a specific period, usually one year.

q: 34. The plan of a building is in the form of a rectangle with centre line dimensions of outer walls as 9.7 m x 14.7 m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30 m. Then its plinth area is
explain: Plinth area = (Length + width of wall) × (Width + width of wall). So, (14.7 + 0.3) × (9.7 + 0.3) = 15.0 × 10.0 = 150 m².

q: 35. While submitting a tender the contractor is required to deposit some amount with the department, as guarantee of the tender known as
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) is a small percentage (usually 1-2%) of the estimated cost paid by the bidder to show interest and prevent frivolous bidding.

q: 36. Provisional sum provided in the bill of quantities is paid to the contractor on the basis of:
explain: A provisional sum is an allowance for work that cannot be fully detailed at the time of tender; it is usually settled based on the actual cost incurred.

q: 37. The Preliminary or Approximate Estimate is prepared based on the:
explain: Preliminary estimates often use the plinth area method, where the total plinth area is multiplied by a known plinth area rate of similar local buildings.

q: 38. Center line method of estimation is mostly used for:
explain: The center line method is a quick and accurate way to calculate quantities for walls and foundations in rectangular or circular buildings.

q: 39. Carpet area does not include the area of
explain: Carpet area is defined as the 'habitable' area. It excludes internal walls, common areas, bathrooms, and external circulation like verandahs.

q: 40. Sludge from a septic tank should be removed in
explain: To maintain the efficiency of the biological process and prevent overflows, it is generally recommended to desludge a septic tank every 1 to 2 years.

q: 41. 'Bill of Quantities' are prepared by .....
explain: Quantity Surveyors (QS) are the professionals specialized in managing all costs relating to building and civil engineering projects, including the preparation of the BOQ.

q: 42. The capacity of septic tank for 100 users will be roughly
explain: For a small number of users (around 10), a septic tank typically requires a capacity of about 7 to 8 cubic meters to allow for proper sedimentation and sludge storage.

q: 43. The necessary elements of a estimates are
explain: To prepare a complete estimate, you require the dimensions from drawings, the quality standards from specifications, and the unit prices (rates) for each item of work.

q: 44. The weight of water per cubic foot is:
explain: One cubic foot of water weighs approximately 62.4 lbs, which converts to roughly 28.31 kgf (rounded to 28.363 in some technical tables).

q: 45. One mile is 1.625km, also it is:
explain: In the Imperial system, 1 mile is exactly equal to 8 furlongs (each furlong being 220 yards).

q: 46. A layer of dry bricks put below the foundation concrete, in the case of soft soils, is called
explain: Soling provides a hard, stable base for the foundation concrete, especially when the underlying soil is soft or has low bearing capacity.

q: 47. A work costing more than Rs. one core is termed as
explain: High-value projects (typically exceeding a specific threshold like 1 Crore) are classified as Major Works requiring higher-level technical and administrative sanction.

q: 48. In the detailed estimate the volumes are worked out to the nearest
explain: According to IS 1200, quantities of volume are generally rounded to the nearest 0.01 cubic meter.

q: 49. When not specified, the volume of steel in R.C.C. work is taken as
explain: For general estimation purposes where exact reinforcement details are missing, the percentage of steel is assumed to be 0.6% to 1.0% for various RC members.

q: 50. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S : 1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: The cross-sectional area consists of a central rectangle (B × d) and two side triangles (each 1/2 × Sd × d), totaling Bd + Sd².
